crombolo site apply

Apply a site package here or to a remote: checked, backed up, one transaction. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo site apply [<bundle>] [--under <under>] [--resolve <resolve>] [--resolve-all <resolve-all>] [--allow-missing-blobs] [--publish] [--no-schema] [--no-files] [--replace-files] [--exclude-people] [--allow-downgrade] [--label <label>] [--backup-taken] [--dry-run] [--save] [--remote <remote>] [--env <env>] [--structure]
ArgumentWhat it is
bundleA site package's directory or .tgz, or `.` for this site's content files.
--underPlace the bundle under this page.
--resolveAnswer a finding: <key>=take-bundle|keep-local|skip, or <key>/<property>[@<culture>]=take-bundle|keep-local.
--resolve-allAnswer every finding the same way. One of take-bundle, keep-local, skip.
--allow-missing-blobsImport media items whose files the bundle does not carry.
--publishPublish what it imports.
--no-schemaDecline the schema the bundle carries.
--no-filesDecline the views, styles and scripts it carries.
--replace-filesAllow replacing files this site has; the originals are kept for a revert.
--exclude-peopleLeave out the members and users it carries; this site's own are untouched.
--allow-downgradeApply a site bundle older than one this site applied from the same signer: a deliberate rollback, recorded in the audit log.
--labelA label for the run.
--backup-takenA backup was taken another way: Postgres needs this, or CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP.
--dry-runSay what it would do, and change nothing.
--saveWith --dry-run: write the answers into the package.
--remoteApply it on this remote instead.
--envWith --remote: the remote's environment.
--structureWith --remote, from a site directory: send its schema, views, styles and code too, not its content alone.

crombolo site build

A site package from a site directory: its schema, views, styles, content and code. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo site build [<dir>] [--template <template>] [--out <out>] [--check] [--public-log] [--sign-with <sign-with>] [--sign] [--name <name>] [--with-media] [--code <code>]
ArgumentWhat it is
dirThe site directory; this one when left out.
--templateA starter site the CLI ships, instead of a directory.
--outThe directory to write it to.
--checkBuild it, report its problems, and write nothing.
--public-logSign from a private repository anyway: Sigstore's public log records its name, workflow, ref and commit.
--sign-withSign it with this user key, as a CI job does, rather than the site's own.
--signSign it once written, in GitHub Actions: `bundle sign` in the same step.
--nameThe site package's name.
--with-mediaThe media files too; left out unless asked.
--codeThe site's own code, as globs; in place of crombolo.code in its package.json.

crombolo site check

What applying a site package would do, here or on a remote, changing nothing. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo site check [<bundle>] [--under <under>] [--resolve <resolve>] [--resolve-all <resolve-all>] [--allow-missing-blobs] [--publish] [--no-schema] [--no-files] [--replace-files] [--exclude-people] [--allow-downgrade] [--label <label>] [--backup-taken] [--dry-run] [--save] [--remote <remote>] [--env <env>] [--structure]
ArgumentWhat it is
bundleA site package's directory or .tgz, or `.` for this site's content files.
--underPlace the bundle under this page.
--resolveAnswer a finding: <key>=take-bundle|keep-local|skip, or <key>/<property>[@<culture>]=take-bundle|keep-local.
--resolve-allAnswer every finding the same way. One of take-bundle, keep-local, skip.
--allow-missing-blobsImport media items whose files the bundle does not carry.
--publishPublish what it imports.
--no-schemaDecline the schema the bundle carries.
--no-filesDecline the views, styles and scripts it carries.
--replace-filesAllow replacing files this site has; the originals are kept for a revert.
--exclude-peopleLeave out the members and users it carries; this site's own are untouched.
--allow-downgradeApply a site bundle older than one this site applied from the same signer: a deliberate rollback, recorded in the audit log.
--labelA label for the run.
--backup-takenA backup was taken another way: Postgres needs this, or CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP.
--dry-runSay what it would do, and change nothing.
--saveWith --dry-run: write the answers into the package.
--remoteApply it on this remote instead.
--envWith --remote: the remote's environment.
--structureWith --remote, from a site directory: send its schema, views, styles and code too, not its content alone.

crombolo site check-code

Check a site package's code against this CMS. Changes nothing.

crombolo site check-code <bundle>
ArgumentWhat it is
bundleThe site package's directory. Required.

crombolo site deploy

Deploy a site directory to a remote: build, check, apply its structure, content and code, restart. Each run acts again.

crombolo site deploy [<dir>] --remote <remote> [--env <env>] [--publish] [--label <label>] [--yes] [--no-restart] [--public-log] [--sign-with <sign-with>] [--sign]
ArgumentWhat it is
dirThe site directory; this one when left out.
--remoteThe remote to deploy to. Required.
--envThe remote's environment.
--publishPublish what it applies.
--labelA label for the run.
--yesDon't ask before applying.
--no-restartApply it and stop: `crombolo restart` makes it live.
--public-logSign from a private repository anyway: Sigstore's public log records its name, workflow, ref and commit.
--sign-withSign it with this user key, rather than the site's own.
--signSign it before sending, in GitHub Actions, for a remote that takes only signed bundles.

crombolo site export

Write the site as a site package, to move it to another machine or host, or a subtree of it. Each run acts again.

crombolo site export [--out <out>] [--subtree <subtree>] [--only] [--with-blueprints] [--with-media] [--drafts] [--with-members] [--with-users] [--with-site-data] [--anonymise] [--name <name>] [--package-version <package-version>] [--include-content] [--allow-content-unencrypted]
ArgumentWhat it is
--outThe file to write; with --subtree, the directory.
--subtreeA subtree to export instead of the whole site; repeatable.
--onlyWith --subtree: the roots alone, not what is below them.
--with-blueprintsWith --subtree: the blueprints of its types.
--with-mediaThe media files too; left out unless asked.
--draftsDrafts too.
--with-membersMembers, encrypted.
--with-usersBack-office users, encrypted.
--with-site-dataThe site's and its extensions' own data, encrypted.
--anonymiseReplace every personal value as it writes.
--nameThe package's npm name.
--package-versionThe package's version.
--include-contentBring property values and media files, encrypted under a passphrase.
--allow-content-unencryptedWith --include-content: write them readable.

crombolo site import

Replace this site with a whole-site package; says what first. Each run acts again.

crombolo site import <file> [--replace] [--replace-all] [--yes] [--allow-missing-media] [--exclude-people] [--backup-taken]
ArgumentWhat it is
fileA whole-site file (crombolo site export). Required.
--replaceReplace this site: what it loses is recycled, people kept.
--replace-allMake it exactly the file: what it loses is deleted, people too.
--yesWith --replace-all: don't ask.
--allow-missing-mediaImport media items whose files the file does not carry.
--exclude-peopleLeave out the members and users it carries; this site's own are untouched.
--backup-takenA backup was taken another way: Postgres needs this, or CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP.

crombolo site key

This site's public key, which signs the site bundles it makes. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo site key

crombolo site revert

Put an import back, restoring what the site served. Each run acts again.

crombolo site revert <run> [--resolve <resolve>] [--resolve-all <resolve-all>] [--force] [--backup-taken] [--remote <remote>] [--env <env>]
ArgumentWhat it is
runThe run id: `crombolo site runs` lists them. Required.
--resolveAnswer a finding: <key>=discard|skip.
--resolve-allAnswer every finding the same way. One of discard, skip.
--forceRevert over changes made since the run.
--backup-takenA backup was taken another way: Postgres needs this, or CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP.
--remoteRevert it on this remote instead.
--envWith --remote: the remote's environment.

crombolo site runs

The site packages applied here or on a remote, and the content extensions brought, newest first. Changes nothing.

crombolo site runs [--limit <limit>] [--offset <offset>] [--fields <fields>] [--remote <remote>] [--env <env>]
ArgumentWhat it is
--limitHow many to list. Default 20.
--offsetHow many to skip first. Default 0.
--fieldsOnly these fields of each item, comma-separated.
--remoteA remote's applies instead.
--envWith --remote: the remote's environment.

crombolo site show

What this site is: its languages, addresses, types, forms, workflows, groups and webhooks. Changes nothing.

crombolo site show

crombolo site urls

Whether page addresses leave out the top-level page. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo site urls [--hide-top-level] [--show-top-level] [--dry-run] [--no-apply]
ArgumentWhat it is
--hide-top-levelLeave the top-level page out of every address.
--show-top-levelPut the top-level page in every address.
--dry-runSay what would change, and change nothing.
--no-applyChange it, and leave applying it to `crombolo types sync`.

crombolo login

Sign in to a remote with a code you approve in its back office. Each run acts again.

crombolo login [<remote>] [--no-browser]
ArgumentWhat it is
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.
--no-browserDon't open the approval page.

crombolo logout

Sign out of a remote, here and at the remote. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo logout [<remote>]
ArgumentWhat it is
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.

crombolo whoami

Who you are signed in as at a remote, and what you may do there. Changes nothing.

crombolo whoami [<remote>]
ArgumentWhat it is
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.

crombolo remote add

A remote this site pulls from and pushes to, kept in remotes.toml. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo remote add <name> <url> [--env <env>] [--force]
ArgumentWhat it is
nameA name for it: lower case letters, digits and dashes. Required.
urlThe site's URL. Required.
--envThe environment it goes to by default.
--forceReplace a remote of the same name.

crombolo remote job

Watch a pull or push job again, after a wait gave up. Changes nothing.

crombolo remote job <id> [<remote>] [--timeout <timeout>]
ArgumentWhat it is
idThe job id the wait printed. Required.
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.
--timeoutSeconds to wait before giving up. Default 1800.

crombolo remote list

The remotes in remotes.toml, and whether you are signed in to each. Changes nothing.

crombolo remote list

crombolo remote remove

Forget a remote; removing one that is not there changes nothing. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo remote remove <name>
ArgumentWhat it is
nameThe remote's name. Required.

crombolo remote trust add

Trust a CI job: its repository and branch, tag or environment, and what it may do. Each run acts again.

crombolo remote trust add [<remote>] --name <name> --provider <provider> --repository <repository> [--branch <branch>] [--tag <tag>] [--environment <environment>] --may <may>
ArgumentWhat it is
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.
--nameWhat to call the rule. Required.
--provider`github`, `gitlab`, or a self-managed GitLab the site names. Required.
--repositoryOwner/name, or group/project. Required.
--branchThe branch the job must run on.
--tagThe tag the job must run on.
--environmentThe CI environment the job must run in.
--mayWhat it may do; repeat for each. One of pull, pull-full, push, push-protected, apply-structure, install-code. Required.

crombolo remote trust disable

Stop a trusted CI job at once; its tokens stop working. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo remote trust disable <rule> [<remote>]
ArgumentWhat it is
ruleThe rule's key, or the start of it. Required.
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.

crombolo remote trust enable

Trust a disabled CI job again. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo remote trust enable <rule> [<remote>]
ArgumentWhat it is
ruleThe rule's key, or the start of it. Required.
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.

crombolo remote trust list

The CI jobs a remote trusts: each rule, what it matches and what it may do. Changes nothing.

crombolo remote trust list [<remote>]
ArgumentWhat it is
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.

crombolo remote trust remove

Forget a trusted CI job; its tokens stop working. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo remote trust remove <rule> [<remote>]
ArgumentWhat it is
ruleThe rule's key, or the start of it. Required.
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.

crombolo pull

A copy of a remote environment: started here, or replacing this site. Each run acts again.

crombolo pull [<remote>] [--env <env>] [--full] [--yes] [--no-media] [--media-info-only] [--lazy-media] [--timeout <timeout>] [--backup-taken]
ArgumentWhat it is
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.
--envThe environment to pull.
--fullA full copy, people included: needs the permission for it.
--yesReplace this site without asking.
--no-mediaLeave the media files out.
--media-info-onlyFetch media files one at a time, only what changed.
--lazy-mediaFetch each media file the first time it is asked for.
--timeoutSeconds to wait for the remote before giving up. Default 1800.
--backup-takenA backup was taken another way: Postgres needs this, or CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP.

crombolo push

Replace a remote environment with this site. Each run acts again.

crombolo push [<remote>] [--env <env>] [--force] [--auto-approve] [--media-info-only] [--dry-run] [--timeout <timeout>] [--no-browser]
ArgumentWhat it is
remoteThe remote; the only one, when there is one.
--envThe environment to replace.
--forceGo on to a protected environment.
--auto-approveWith --force: don't ask for its name.
--media-info-onlySend media files one at a time, only what the remote lacks.
--dry-runSay what it would replace, and send nothing.
--timeoutSeconds to wait for the remote before giving up. Default 1800.
--no-browserDon't open an approval page.

crombolo extension build

Build a bundle made in the Bundle Editor as an extension package. Each run acts again.

crombolo extension build <name> [--out <out>] [--with-media] [--check]
ArgumentWhat it is
nameThe definition's name or id. Required.
--outThe file to write; named for the package when left out.
--with-mediaThe media files its picks name.
--checkBuild it and say what it holds, writing nothing.

crombolo extension check

Check an extension package before publishing or installing it. Changes nothing.

crombolo extension check <bundle>
ArgumentWhat it is
bundleThe package directory or .tgz. Required.

crombolo extension disable

Turn a bundle's server features off, here or on a remote. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo extension disable <name> [--remote <remote>] [--env <env>]
ArgumentWhat it is
nameThe bundle id or its package name. Required.
--remoteOn this remote instead.
--envWith --remote: the remote's environment.

crombolo extension enable

Turn a disabled bundle's server features back on, here or on a remote. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo extension enable <name> [--remote <remote>] [--env <env>]
ArgumentWhat it is
nameThe bundle id or its package name. Required.
--remoteOn this remote instead.
--envWith --remote: the remote's environment.

crombolo extension grant

Grant an installed extension what it asks for, here or on a remote. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo extension grant <name> [--grant <grant>] [--act-as <act-as>] [--remote <remote>] [--env <env>]
ArgumentWhat it is
nameThe package name, or its bundle id. Required.
--grantA permission it asks for; name every one.
--act-asWith actAs: whom it acts for, the calling user or a named one.
--remoteGrant it on this remote instead.
--envWith --remote: the remote's environment.

crombolo extension install

Add an extension to this site, or a remote, as a dependency. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo extension install <bundle> [--grant <grant>] [--act-as <act-as>] [--apply-content] [--layout <layout>] [--code-into <code-into>] [--remote <remote>] [--env <env>] [--dry-run]
ArgumentWhat it is
bundleA package name, name@version, a packed .tgz, or with --code-into a site package. Required.
--grantA permission it asks for; name every one.
--act-asWith actAs: whom it acts for, the calling user or a named one.
--apply-contentApply the content it carries too.
--layoutThe site's layout its page templates sit in.
--code-intoInstall a site package's own code into this empty directory.
--remoteInstall it on this remote instead.
--envWith --remote: the remote's environment.
--dry-runSay what it would install and grant; install nothing.

crombolo extension list

The bundles this site, or a remote, has installed. Changes nothing.

crombolo extension list [--remote <remote>] [--env <env>]
ArgumentWhat it is
--remoteA remote's bundles instead.
--envWith --remote: the remote's environment.

crombolo extension migrate

Rewrite an extension's package to the layout this release takes. Each run acts again.

crombolo extension migrate <dir> [--reason <reason>] [--dry-run]
ArgumentWhat it is
dirThe extension's package directory. Required.
--reasonWhy its back-office code is needed, shown when it is installed.
--dry-runSay what would move, and write nothing.

crombolo extension purge

Back up, then drop a bundle's tables and clear its state. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo extension purge <id> [--yes] [--dry-run] [--backup-taken]
ArgumentWhat it is
idThe bundle's id. Required.
--yesDon't ask: drop them.
--dry-runSay what it would do, and change nothing.
--backup-takenA backup was taken another way: Postgres needs this, or CROMBOLO_PG_DUMP.

crombolo extension settings

Read an installed extension's settings, or set them. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo extension settings <name>
ArgumentWhat it is
nameThe package name, or its bundle id. Required.

crombolo extension uninstall

Remove an installed extension, here or on a remote. Each run acts again.

crombolo extension uninstall <name> [--remote <remote>] [--env <env>] [--revert-content]
ArgumentWhat it is
nameThe package name. Required.
--remoteRemove it on this remote instead.
--envWith --remote: the remote's environment.
--revert-contentFirst put back the content its install applied; nothing is removed if that is refused.

crombolo bundle digest

Print the digest a bundle's signature covers. Changes nothing.

crombolo bundle digest <bundle>
ArgumentWhat it is
bundleA package directory, a .tgz, a URL, or name@version on the registry. Required.

crombolo bundle sign

Sign a bundle in GitHub Actions, from the commit or tag it was built at. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo bundle sign <bundle> [--public-log]
ArgumentWhat it is
bundleThe package directory or .tgz. Required.
--public-logSign from a private repository anyway: Sigstore's public log records its name, workflow, ref and commit.

crombolo bundle verify

Check where a bundle was built, without installing it. Changes nothing.

crombolo bundle verify <bundle> [--require] [--source <source>]
ArgumentWhat it is
bundleA package directory, a .tgz, a URL, or name@version on the registry. Required.
--requireRefuse an unsigned bundle.
--sourceRefuse a signed bundle built anywhere but here: org/*, org/repo or org/repo@<tags>.

crombolo keys create

Make a key of your own, on this machine, to sign site bundles with. Each run acts again.

crombolo keys create <name> [--comment <comment>]
ArgumentWhat it is
nameWhat to call it here: lowercase, digits and hyphens. Required.
--commentThe name sites see beside it; its name by default.

crombolo keys list

The keys of your own on this machine, with their public lines. Changes nothing.

crombolo keys list

crombolo keys trust

Trust a key, or a CI build, to sign the site bundles this site applies. Each run acts again.

crombolo keys trust <name> [<publicKey>] [--site] [--source <source>] [--bundle <bundle>]
ArgumentWhat it is
nameWhat to call it on the list. Required.
publicKeyThe key's public line.
--siteIt is another site's key, not a person's.
--sourceTrust builds of this repository instead: owner/repo, owner/*, or @ a tag pattern.
--bundleTrust the key that signed this bundle, once its signature checks out.

crombolo keys trusted

The keys and CI builds this site trusts to sign the site bundles it applies. Changes nothing.

crombolo keys trusted

crombolo keys untrust

Stop trusting a key or a CI build: site bundles it signed are refused from now on. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo keys untrust <signer>
ArgumentWhat it is
signerIts fingerprint, its repository, or its name on the list. Required.

values.value: the command line’s own description of its commands
Move a site as a site package, install extensions, and sign in to another environment to pull from and push to.
